tools.name: propose_theme
tools.description: Give the Sanduhr widget a new color theme. Call when the user asks for a theme, a new look, or colors from an image, a palette, or a vibe. Write the palette per docs/themes/AGENT_PROMPT.md: fourteen role-named #rrggbb colors (bg, glass, glass_on_mica, title_bg, border, footer_bg, bar_bg, text, text_secondary, text_dim, text_muted, accent, pace_marker, sparkline) plus name and optional dials (glass_alpha 0.7-0.9, border_alpha 0.2-0.6, border_tint, accent_bloom, inner_highlight). Rules: dark base (bg/glass luminance under 0.25); text at 4.5:1 or better on the card; text_secondary, text_dim, text_muted the same hue as text at decreasing luminance; one accent hue shared by accent, sparkline and border_tint; pace_marker visible on every bar fill (a complementary hue works). Optional: font (a font family the widget's text, and the Desk while it follows the theme, is drawn in) and desk {ink, bars, message: 1 to 4 #rrggbb each; glow, plate_color, shadow: #rrggbb; plate: true or false; font}: the Desk's look for this theme, every field optional with a default worked out from the colors; bars also fills the widget's bars, with a yellow or red middle stop at the user's alert levels. The server lints first: status rejected with findings means fix the named fields and call again, nothing was written. Otherwise the widget saves the theme under its themes folder and applies it (apply: false saves without switching); the result names the previous theme's key so the user can go back, and carries any warnings.

theme.description: The palette JSON: name, the fourteen #rrggbb colors, optional dials, optional font and desk.

save_as.description: File key under the themes folder. Default: the name, slugged.

tools.name: get_desk_messages
tools.description: Read the user's Desk messages: the handwritten line Sanduhr draws on the Windows desktop, picked from %APPDATA%\Sanduhr\messages.txt. Returns every raw line of the file (comments and effects included), whether one line is pinned, the rotation (daily or hourly), mix_daily (whether plain lines take turns with a weekday's own lines), today: the usual raw line the Desk shows now, and today_special: the date lines it shows above it today (empty on most days). Call this before propose_desk_messages to match the user's voice and to avoid repeats. messages.txt syntax, one line each: a plain line shows on any day; 'Mon: text' only on that weekday (Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat Sun, exactly so); '10-31: text' only on that date (MM-DD); '# text' is a comment and blank lines are ignored. Each day the Desk shows one usual line: today's weekday lines if there are any (they replace the plain lines that day, unless the user's mix_daily switch is on, which lets the plain lines take turns with them), else the plain lines; it rotates through them once a day (a weekday's lines once a week) or once an hour (rotate, the user's choice), steady in between. Date lines are special days: they do not replace the usual line, they add to it, drawn above it, and every line for that date shows (two birthdays on one date both show; more than 3 take turns hourly, 3 at a time). So birthdays, anniversaries and holidays are date lines, one per person or occasion, short and friendly, like '03-14: {ink:#ff7e5f,#feb47b} happy birthday, Sam.'; the user's everyday line still shows under them. Pinning one line is a user setting (pinned): the pinned line replaces the usual line every day, so weekday and plain lines don't show while it is pinned (say so before proposing them), but date lines still stack above the pinned line, so birthdays and holidays show either way. The user's On special days setting (special_mode) decides how the date's lines share the Desk with the usual line: stack (all at once, the date's lines on top), turns (one at a time, crossfading) or scroll (one at a time, gliding up like a slow ticker), each line shown for special_seconds. Effects: tags at the start of the text, after any prefix, in any order, each in braces: {ink:#ff2a6d,#05d9e8} this line's ink, 1 to 4 hex colors (2 or more make a left-to-right gradient); {glow} / {noglow} turn the soft glow on or off for this line; {size:1.3} scales the line from 0.5 to 2 times the Desk's message size; {write} draws the line in, left to right like handwriting, once when it first appears; {shimmer} sends a slow light sweep across it every few seconds; {sweep} runs a three-character light across the line that brightens it toward white, once when the line appears, and {sweep:20} every 20 seconds (2 to 3600); {font:small-caps} draws the line in a letter style: bold, italic, bold-italic and small-caps in the Desk's own font (its weight, a slant, small capitals), sans, mono, double-struck, script and fraktur as Unicode math letters (A to Z, a to z and, where the style has them, digits; accents and punctuation stay as written). Examples: '{ink:#ffd08a} showtime.', 'Fri: {ink:#ff2a6d,#05d9e8} {glow} ship it.', '10-31: {ink:#ff7518,#6b2fa0} {write} happy halloween.', '{size:0.8} {noglow} breathe.', '{font:small-caps} {sweep} showtime.', '{font:script} {sweep:30} good morning.'. Good taste: short lines (handwriting reads best under about 40 characters, two lines at most on screen), lowercase and a period suit the hand, {write}, {shimmer} and {sweep} sparingly (a few lines, not every line, and one of them per line), {font:...} on short lines, gradients with 2 or 3 colors that sit near each other, sizes near 1. With animations turned off in Windows, {write} shows at once and {shimmer} and {sweep} are skipped.

lines.description: The lines, exactly as they would sit in messages.txt (prefix first, then effects, then the text).

mode.description: add appends the lines (lines already in the list are skipped); replace swaps the whole list for them (the comment block at the top of the file stays). Default add.

note.description: One short sentence for the user on why these lines (shown beside the suggestion).

tools.name: get_desk
tools.description: Read the user's Desk before designing it. The Desk is what Sanduhr draws on the Windows desktop: a clock, Claude usage, a handwritten message, a Launcher of buttons, a sprite companion and other pieces, each placed at one of eight anchors (tl tc tr ml mr bl bc br) with a size, in a font and an ink, optionally on a soft plate, beside the widget's color theme. Returns design (the current look as a full design: layout with every piece's anchor, size, hidden, monitor and tilt (the slant of its stack in degrees, 0 upright), and for claude, meters and telemetry its style (bar, slim, ring or ticks; limits.piece_style lists the pieces and the words), weather.nickname (the name the weather piece shows instead of the place's, "" for none), font, ink, plate, shadow, launcher, theme, follows_theme: true while the Desk draws the theme's look instead of its own), theme_look (that look worked out from the theme: gradient, ink, bars, message, glow, plate, plate_color, shadow, font, bar_track, pace_tick), pieces and anchors (the allowed words), fonts (installed families, and the bundled handwriting fonts EsteFont Pro and EsteFont 26), wallpaper (path of a copy of the wallpaper image scaled to at most 1600 pixels on its longest side, which you can open only if the user allows Claude Code to read that file; source file, or cache when Windows' cached copy stands in for a wallpaper file that was deleted; kind image, or color when the shell names no image and the summary is the desktop's background color; and summary: overall brightness 0-1, up to five dominant colors with their share, and for each monitor the brightness 0-1 and busyness 0-1 (edge density) behind each anchor), designs (saved designs: id, name, pinned, applied_at), direct (true when the user lets Claude change the Desk without review), limits, and start_menu_apps (the apps a Launcher button may open, as id and name; absent until Sanduhr has read the Start menu). Call this before propose_desk and design from what it says. status no_data with reason missing means the Sanduhr widget is not running or its Claude Code integration is not installed.

tools.name: propose_desk
tools.description: Propose a look for the user's Desk, and optionally the widget's color theme. The design is PARTIAL: send only the fields to change; everything absent stays as it is. Fields, all optional: name (up to 40 characters); note (one sentence for the user, up to 200); layout {piece: {anchor, size, hidden}}, where piece is a key from get_desk pieces, anchor is tl tc tr ml mr bl bc br, size is 0.6 to 1.6, hidden removes the piece and monitor puts it on "all" monitors (the default), the "main" monitor or one monitor by the id in get_desk monitors (a piece on a monitor that is unplugged shows on the main one meanwhile; the companion piece draws the sprite the user chose in Settings, Desk, Pieces, sits at its anchor or roams the monitor's edges from it, and draws nothing until a sprite is installed); tilt in a layout piece slants the piece's whole stack from -20 to 20 degrees (negative rises to the right, positive falls; 0 upright), so a left stack at -18 and a right stack at 18 read as two faces of a fold; pieces at one anchor share one slant, so give them the same tilt; style in a layout piece, only on claude, meters and telemetry, is how its numbers draw so a stack fits its column: bar (the default, a full-width bar with its label above), slim (label and value on one line over a thin bar, about half the height; claude becomes a compact two-row line), ring (small arc gauges with the value inside, side by side in a row), ticks (ten segmented cells, the OLED-friendly one); a Claude limit keeps its pace mark in every style, and slim or ring keep a dense or slanted stack from running wide; weather {nickname} (up to 24 characters, shown on the Desk's weather piece instead of the place's name, "" for the place's own name; it never leaves the PC and the forecast still uses the city the user picked); font (a family from get_desk fonts.installed or the bundled EsteFont Pro or EsteFont 26, or {family, link} with an https link to get a font the user lacks: Sanduhr never downloads it, the review shows the link and Apply waits for the font, status needs_font); ink (auto, light, dark, theme, one #rrggbb, or a list of 2 to 4 #rrggbb for a left-to-right gradient); plate and shadow (true or false; the plate is a soft panel behind each stack of pieces); launcher {orientation row or column, buttons: up to 8 of {kind app or link, target, label up to 24 characters, glow #rrggbb}}, where an app target is an id from get_desk start_menu_apps (a button opens only what the Start menu lists; there are no command lines) and a link target is an https link; messages {lines, mode add or replace}, the lines as propose_desk_messages takes them (see its description for the syntax); looks (up to 20 per-song looks for the now playing line, {title, artist, ink, style, mood} as propose_now_playing_looks takes them, saved with the design when it is applied; each color must keep 3:1 against what is behind the now playing piece, and they show while the user's Style what's playing is on); theme (a widget palette: name and the fourteen #rrggbb colors, per docs/themes/AGENT_PROMPT.md, as propose_theme takes it, with its optional font and desk look); follows_theme (true draws the Desk in the theme's look; its ink is judged by its first stop, and the Desk turns its plate on where that would not read). The server checks before anything is sent: every field's shape and range; ink against the wallpaper (each placed piece's ink must keep a WCAG contrast of at least 3:1 against the wallpaper brightness under its anchor on every monitor, or against the plate when the plate is on; auto ink picks its own and is not judged), so read get_desk wallpaper.summary and choose ink, plate and anchors together; the Launcher's targets; the message lines; the theme lint. status rejected comes with reasons, each {field, message}: fix those fields and call again; nothing was written. Otherwise the Sanduhr widget draws the design live on the desktop with a bar where the user chooses Apply or Dismiss: previewing means the user is reviewing it now (do not send the same look again), applied means it is in place (the user allows direct changes; their previous look is saved), needs_font lists the fonts (family, link) the user must install first, queued means the widget did not answer and will show it when it starts. Every applied look is saved and can be switched back to in Sanduhr's settings. This server never changes the Desk itself.

design.description: A partial Desk design: only the fields to change. See the tool description for each field.

layout.description: Piece key (from get_desk pieces) to {anchor: tl|tc|tr|ml|mr|bl|bc|br, size: 0.6-1.6, hidden: boolean, monitor: all|main|a monitor id from get_desk monitors, tilt: -20 to 20 degrees, the slant of the piece's whole stack, style: bar|slim|ring|ticks, only on claude, meters and telemetry}.

weather.description: {nickname: up to 24 characters}: the name the weather piece shows instead of the place's own; "" goes back to the place's name. Local only; the forecast keeps the city's coordinates.

font.description: A font family name, or {family, link} with an https link to get a font the user lacks.

ink.description: auto, light, dark, theme, one #rrggbb color, or a list of 2 to 4 #rrggbb colors (gradient).

launcher.description: {orientation: row|column, buttons: up to 8 of {kind: app|link, target, label, glow}}. An app target is an id from get_desk start_menu_apps; a link is https.

messages.description: {lines: [...], mode: add|replace}, the lines as propose_desk_messages takes them.

looks.description: Per-song looks for the now playing line, up to 20 of {title, artist, ink, style, mood}, as propose_now_playing_looks takes them.

theme.description: A widget palette as propose_theme takes it: name and the fourteen #rrggbb colors, optional font and desk.

follows_theme.description: True draws the Desk in the widget theme's own look (get_desk theme_look) instead of its font, ink and plate.

note.description: One short sentence for the user on why this look (shown in the review bar; overrides design.note).

tools.name: propose_now_playing_looks
tools.description: Suggest a look for songs the user plays: a gradient and a letter style per song, drawn on the now playing line of the user's Windows Desk while Sanduhr's Style what's playing is on (Settings, Now playing, Looks). Until a song has a look it wears one picked from its name out of eight palettes. Pass looks: 1 to 20 of {title, artist, ink, style, mood}: title and artist exactly as the player shows them (matched ignoring case, extra spaces and a trailing Remastered mark), ink 1 to 4 #rrggbb colors left to right (a gradient across the line), style one of plain, bold, italic, bolditalic or smallcaps (omit for plain; drawn in the Desk's own font), mood up to 40 characters for the user ('neon night drive'). Every color must keep a WCAG contrast of 3:1 against what is behind the now playing piece, the wallpaper under its anchor or the plate when the plate is on, so no dark shades on a dark wallpaper and no pale ones on a bright one; read get_desk (wallpaper summary and layout) first. Refused looks come back as rejected with reasons, each starting with the look's number, and nothing is sent. Pick songs you know the user plays (they said so, or ask them); a look should feel like the song: its era, its cover, its energy. Sanduhr checks the looks again and, unless the user lets Claude style songs directly, shows them as a card to Save or Dismiss: pending_approval means the user decides, applied means they are saved (looks_saved), rejected comes with reasons. style_on says whether Style what's playing is on; when it is false, tell the user where to switch it on (Settings, Now playing, Looks). A saved look replaces an older one for the same song. queued means Sanduhr did not answer: it is not running. This server never saves a look and never reads what is playing.

ink.description: 1 to 4 hex colors, left to right, each 3:1 or better on what is behind the now playing piece.

mood.description: A few words for the user ("neon night drive").

note.description: One short sentence for the user on why these looks (shown beside the suggestion).

tools.name: propose_widget
tools.description: Make a widget for the user's Sanduhr Desk with them: a pixel-art companion sprite, a palette pack for the Desk ink, or an effects pack. Call when the user asks for a desk pet, a companion, a sprite, a palette or an effect preset. The pack is data only: never a PNG, never a font, never code. A widget theme goes through propose_theme instead. Pass kind, pack {id, name (1-40), description (1-200), version?, author?, license?} and the kind's files. Sanduhr namespaces the id my-<id>, writes pack.json and a LICENSE (CC0-1.0 by default), validates the whole pack with the catalog's own rules (strict), and refuses with status rejected and reasons before anything is sent. Trademark rule: no 'claude' or 'anthropic' anywhere and no 'opus', 'sonnet', 'haiku' or 'fable' as words, in any name, description, author, file name or JSON string; original art only, no studio or game characters. SPRITE: sprite = sprite.json, schema_version 2: frame_w and frame_h (8 to 32 for pixel sheets), scale 1-4 (nearest neighbour), fps 1-24, either sheet (one .json path) or stages (1-6 of {id kebab 2-20, name 1-24, min_growth 0 for the first then strictly increasing up to 1, sheet, frame_w, frame_h}; stage 0's size equals the top-level size; stages grow with the user's coding days, never tokens), animations (name to 1-64 frame indexes; required: walk, sit, nap, pop, cheer, worry, focus, sleep, celebrate), moods {content, focused, worried, exhausted, celebrate} and triggers {needs_you, job_passed, near_limit, idle} each naming an animation, roam {edges: subset of bottom, left, right; speed_px_s 5-120}. sheets = path to a pixel sheet: {palette: 1-16 '#rrggbb' colors, never #ffffff (use #f0f0f0), frame_w, frame_h (equal to the stage's), frames: 1-256 frames, each exactly frame_h strings of exactly frame_w characters, top row first; '.' is transparent and 0-9, a-f (lowercase) index the palette}. Frame i is frames[i]; every sheet needs a frame for the highest index any animation uses. Keep the character on transparency, readable at scale 2, and give walk two or more frames. PALETTE: palettes = 1-64 of {name: lowercase-kebab 2-24, unique; colors: 1-4 '#rrggbb' stops left to right; mood? up to 24 characters}. EFFECTS: effects = 1-64 of {name as for palettes, type glow|sweep|shimmer|pulse, intensity 0-1, period_ms integer 400-10000, color '#rrggbb' or 'ink'}. Sanduhr checks the pack again and previews it on the Desk (a sprite as the companion, a palette as the Desk ink) with a review bar: previewing means the user is looking at it; it installs only when they press Apply (applied, as a local widget made here, listed in Settings, Mods & Widgets, Installed; companion true when they made a sprite the companion), and Dismiss answers rejected with reason dismissed and writes nothing. 'Let Claude change the Desk directly' does not cover widgets: a new pack always waits for Apply. queued means Sanduhr did not answer: it is not running. Nothing is uploaded; sharing a pack is a pull request to the sanduhr-widgets catalog.

kind.description: What the pack is. A widget theme goes through propose_theme instead; fonts are never proposed.

pack.description: pack.json's own fields. Sanduhr writes files, kind, schema_version and sanduhr_min, and the LICENSE text.

id.description: Lowercase kebab-case; Sanduhr prefixes my- (3 to 40 characters with it).

author.description: Default: Made here. Never a brand or model name.

license.description: Default CC0-1.0. Sanduhr writes the matching LICENSE.

sprite.description: kind sprite: sprite.json (schema_version 2): frame_w, frame_h, scale, fps, sheet or stages, animations, moods, triggers, roam. Every sheet path ends .json and is a key of sheets.

sheets.description: kind sprite: pixel sheets, path (such as sheet.json or sprites/egg.json) to {palette, frame_w, frame_h, frames}.

palettes.description: kind palette: palettes.json, {schema_version: 1, palettes: [...]} or the list alone.

effects.description: kind effects: effects.json, {schema_version: 1, effects: [...]} or the list alone.

note.description: One short sentence for the user on what you made and why (shown on the review bar).
